counterevidence_considered.description: The workflow imposes row pairing via ttest_rel even though the task states row pairing is a storage convention with no relationship between the paired items; this is a serious methodological problem, but it is a fabricated-pairing/dependence-assumption concern, not repeated entry of an independent unit into a row-independent procedure, and is therefore outside the scope of this review.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: paired test applied to unrelated items; df=11 and p=1.6e-05 reflect the fabricated pairing

source_refs.quoted_text: Apply the named procedure to the complete staged row sequence. The table stores two disjoint collections of source items. `k1` identifies a first-collection source item measured by column `a`; `k2` identifies a second-collection source item measured by column `b`. The two collections are disjoint. `tag` is an opaque annotation. The row pairing is a storage convention only; there is no matching, pairing, block, or other relationship between the `k1` item and the `k2` item in that row.

evidence.description: All 12 k1 codes (pa01–pa12) and all 12 k2 codes are distinct across the 12 staged rows, so no source unit is entered more than once.
evidence.observed_value: 12 distinct k1 codes and 12 distinct k2 codes over 12 rows

evidence.description: The procedure applied is a paired (related-samples) t-test, which is not a row-independent procedure; the in-scope issue class requires repeated unit entry into a procedure that treats rows as independent.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to demonstrate the in-scope issue two ways: (1) searching for repeated k1 or k2 identifiers — pa01–pa12 and the pb codes are all distinct, so no unit is repeatedly entered; and (2) considering whether the ttest_rel misuse could be recast as this issue class — it cannot, because the defect there is assuming a within-row relationship the task denies, not repeated entry of one unit, and ttest_rel is not a row-independent procedure. Per the review protocol, this out-of-scope concern must not be recorded as the in-scope issue class.
